question.text: Under the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008, when the designated authority has recommended cancellation of registration or the competent authority is prima facie of the view that it is a fit case for cancellation, what opportunity may the competent authority grant?

answer.text: An opportunity to transfer the registration to another entity
An opportunity to negotiate a settlement amount
An opportunity to submit a written appeal to the Supreme Court

explanation.text: The Logic: The competent authority may grant an opportunity of personal hearing where the designated authority has recommended cancellation of the certificate of registration, or where the competent authority is prima facie of the view that it is a fit case for cancellation. The Trap: The source uses "may" rather than "must" — personal hearing in cancellation cases is an opportunity the competent authority can grant, not an automatic mandatory step. Transfer of registration, settlement and direct Supreme Court appeal are not part of this stage. Note: Appeals to higher fora (SAT and then the Supreme Court) come later in the remedial chain, not within these proceedings.
